acceptanceCriteria: Root cause confirmed: either the test's survivor check races a legitimate but slow process exit under load (test timing defect), or an interrupted run really leaves a child alive past the stop boundary (product defect).
`GOTOOLCHAIN=local go test -count=20 -run TestATRV0004_InterruptStopsTheRun ./internal/tasks/cli/` passes under concurrent host load (load average comparable to 40+).
If it is a product defect, a regression test proves that no child survives an interrupted run; if it is test-only, the survivor wait is bounded by an observed exit, not a fixed sleep.
body:
Observed 2026-10-05 by the V1-0755 lane agent (Claude Code supervisor host, branch claude/v1-0755-claude-code-host at 3992d096) and reported to the orchestrator. Go 1.27.1 darwin/arm64.

TestATRV0004_InterruptStopsTheRun in internal/tasks/cli failed with SURVIVORS under load, at load average 43-53 with sibling lanes running package tests. It also fails 2 of 15 on the unchanged base ce4ae150, so V1-0755 did not cause it. It passes when run alone.

Expected: the test is deterministic under load, and no child survives an interrupted run. Actual: the survivor check sometimes reports live processes.

Unconfirmed: whether this is a test timing defect or a real survivor. Related timing-flake classes: V1-0534 (qualify-opencode, completed) and V1-0766 (tracerecordrepo TempDir cleanup).
title: tests: TestATRV0004_InterruptStopsTheRun reports SURVIVORS under host load
